text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a spike of dropped connections when we fail traffic from eu-west -> us-west during regional pin fallback. Affected cluster = gpu-inference-eu-prod, several p95 timeouts and model RPC failures.
simon: Reproed locally with a small load test. Saw `nf_conntrack: table full` messages on the NAT instances. Logs: 
```
Mar 18 18:12:04 nat-gw-3 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Mar 18 18:12:05 nat-gw-3 kernel: nf_conntrack: lowmem, dropping conntrack entry
```
zara: Confirmed — when we push to us-west via geo-fallback the source IPs change and conntrack spikes (many ephemeral client connections + short keep-alives from inference clients).
kai: How big are the conntrack tables right now?
simon: On the NAT boxes `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` = 262144. But `conntrack -L | wc -l` was ~255k at peak. Hitting the limit.
maya: Are these GPU workers opening many outbound connections to model repos / telemetry or is it client traffic?
simon: Mostly client traffic. Each model worker (avx2 inference) opens many concurrent HTTP/1.1 connections for inference shards. Keep-alive is short (2s) so churn is huge during spikes.
kai: Two mitigation paths: (1) increase nf_conntrack_max on NAT instances (RAM cost), (2) reduce unique source IP churn by using stable egress pools or SNAT affinity, (3) make clients multiplex more (HTTP/2) or increase keep-alive.
zara: We also observed that when conntrack starts evicting entries the ALB healthchecks see connections reset -> LB rebalances -> more cold starts on GPU instances. So it cascades and increases GPU load/cost.
maya: That explains the weird CPU/GPU utilization pattern during failover — more model restarts because of perceived unhealthy backends.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-18T18:20: alert_id=INC-4891 service=nat-gateways severity=high — conntrack saturation detected on eu-west nat cluster.
simon: Quick temporary fix: bump nf_conntrack_max to 524288 and enable `nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal=1`? Also tune `hashsize`. I'll open a canary PR to the bootstrap-config for the NAT ASG.
kai: Bumping helps short-term but has cost: more memory per NAT instance and if we hit it again we still have cascading effects. Longer-term we should avoid cross-region SNAT churn. Proposal: pin inference outbound for eu-west traffic to eu-wide egress pool even when routing fallback goes to us-west model endpoints (i.e., use regional egress stitching).
zara: Implementation options: per-region egress proxies (sticky IPs) or use GRPC/http proxy in-region that forwards to remote region but preserves source. Both add latency but avoid conntrack explosion.
maya: Tradeoffs: pinned egress preserves connection stability (lower GPU churn) but increases cross-region bandwidth and egress costs. We'll need to model bandwidth cost vs. GPU restart cost.
simon: I'll run a cost estimate: assume 10TB/day cross-region if we pin egress vs current 1TB/day when failing over (because currently many requests drop).
kai: Also check load balancer idle timeout and client keep-alive. If ALB idle timeout is 60s but clients close after 2s we get more conn churn. Maybe increase ALB idle to 120s for inference routes.
maya: Action items: 1) simon to roll conntrack bump to canary NAT group and monitor (ETA 30m). 2) kai + zara to prototype regional egress pinning design and cost model (ETA EOD). 3) devex to message SDK teams to increase keep-alive/HTTP/2 usage for inference clients.
simon: Rolling now to nat-gw-group-a canary. Will post metrics (conntrack usage, TCP resets) once done. :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks — if we see recurrence we'll escalate to dedicated regional egress gateways for inference traffic and consider adding a small LRU TCP proxy in front of GPU workers.
oncall-bot: ACTION LOGGED: INC-4891 assigned to simon; priority=high; sla=4h
